artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each positive integer $n$ define
$$a_n := \frac{1}{n(2n+1)\binom{2n}{n}}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(6k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^{2}\binom{3k}{k}\,6^{3(n-1-k)},$$
$$b_n := \frac{1}{2n(2n+1)\binom{2n}{n}}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(8k+1)\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}\,48^{2(n-1-k)},$$
where $\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}=(4k)!/(k!)^4$.

(i) Prove that for every integer $n>1$ one has $a_n,b_n\in\mathbb{Z}$, except when $2n+1$ is a power of $3$, in which case $3a_n,3b_n\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus 3\mathbb{Z}$.

(ii) Let $p>3$ be a prime and let $\left(\frac{\cdot}{p}\right)$ denote the Legendre symbol. Prove that
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^2\binom{3k}{k}}{6^{3k}}\equiv\begin{cases}4x^{2}-2p\pmod{p^{2}}&\text{if }p\equiv 1,7\pmod{24},\ p=x^{2}+6y^{2},\\ 8x^{2}-2p\pmod{p^{2}}&\text{if }p\equiv 5,11\pmod{24},\ p=2x^{2}+3y^{2},\\ 0\pmod{p^{2}}&\text{if }\left(\tfrac{-6}{p}\right)=-1,\end{cases}$$
and
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}}{48^{2k}}\equiv\begin{cases}4x^{2}-2p\pmod{p^{2}}&\text{if }p\equiv 1,7\pmod{24},\ p=x^{2}+6y^{2},\\ 2p-8x^{2}\pmod{p^{2}}&\text{if }p\equiv 5,11\pmod{24},\ p=2x^{2}+3y^{2},\\ 0\pmod{p^{2}}&\text{if }\left(\tfrac{-6}{p}\right)=-1,\end{cases}$$
where $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$ are as indicated.

Furthermore, prove that for every prime $p>3$ and every $a\in\mathbb{Z}^{+}$,
$$p^{a}\sum_{k=0}^{p^{a}-1}\frac{6k+1}{6^{3k}}\binom{2k}{k}^{2}\binom{3k}{k}\equiv (p^{a}-p^{a-1})\,\tfrac{5}{12}\,p^{2}B_{p-2}(1)\pmod{p^{3}},$$
$$p^{a}\sum_{k=0}^{p^{a}-1}\frac{8k+1}{48^{2k}}\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}\equiv(p^{a}-p^{a-1})\,\tfrac{5}{24}\,p^{2}B_{p-2}(1)\pmod{p^{3}},$$
$$p^{a}\sum_{p^{a}/2<k<p^{a}}\frac{8k+1}{48^{2k}}\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}\equiv 0\pmod{p^{2}},$$
where $B_{n}(x)$ denotes the $n$th Bernoulli polynomial.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches reveal that several Sun-type supercongruence conjectures involving central binomial coefficients have been proved (e.g., works of Guo, Z.-H. Sun, and via the Wilf–Zeilberger method), and there is active literature on related congruences modulo $p^2$ and $p^3$. However, no source explicitly confirming a complete proof of the specific conjecture (with the integrality assertion (i) and the full $p^2$/$p^3$ congruences in (ii) for the sums with weight $63^{-k}\binom{2k}{k}^2\binom{3k}{k}$ and $48^{-2k}\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}$) was located, so the status is taken to be unknown.

status_evidence.title: On a supercongruence conjecture of Z.-W. Sun
status_evidence.snippet: Researchers have proven supercongruences conjectured by Z.-W. Sun via various methods.
status_evidence.claim: Several of Sun's supercongruence conjectures have been resolved, but the specific conjecture in question is not directly addressed.

status_evidence.title: Proof of Sun's conjectures on super congruences and the divisibility of certain binomial sums
status_evidence.snippet: Proof of Sun's conjectures on super congruences and the divisibility of certain binomial sums.
status_evidence.claim: Some related Sun conjectures on integrality and supercongruences are proved, but coverage of this specific A14 conjecture was not confirmed.
